claim: MWAA completed an ALP amendment, NEPA Environmental Assessment, and FAA coordination to develop 424 acres of Dulles airport land for data centers in 2018, establishing direct internal precedent for the current proposal
source_title: Airports Authority Announces Sale of 424 Acres of Western Lands at Dulles International
supporting_excerpt: With no future airport uses envisioned for this undeveloped land, the Airports Authority sought to lease or sell the 424 acres to realize a return on the earlier investment... The change to the Dulles Airport Layout Plan (ALP) is subject to the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), which requires evaluation of the environmental impacts of proposed federal actions, and an Environmental Assessment is being prepared in accordance with FAA policies and procedures.
caveat: This was for property immediately adjacent to but outside the airfield boundary; the current proposal is within the airport fence. The distinction matters but the ALP/NEPA process is the same.

claim: MWAA sold the Western Lands to Digital Realty for $236.5 million, revenue restricted to aeronautical purposes, demonstrating FAA and grant assurance compliance is achievable for data center development on airport property
source_title: Dulles Land Buy Gives Digital Realty Runway for Data Center Expansion
supporting_excerpt: Digital Realty signed a letter of intent to acquire a 433-acre property from the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority (MWAA) for $236.5 million. Revenue from the sale can only be used by the Airports Authority for aeronautical purposes at Dulles International.
caveat: Trade press summary; primary source is MWAA board resolution and transaction documents not publicly available in full text.

claim: FAA AIM § 7-6-16 defines exhaust plumes as emissions from 'power plants, industrial production facilities, or other industrial systems that release large amounts of vertically directed unstable gases' — data centers and commercial HVAC systems are not covered
source_title: AIM § 7-6-16 Avoid Flight in the Vicinity of Exhaust Plumes (Smoke Stacks and Cooling Towers)
supporting_excerpt: Exhaust plumes [are] visible or invisible emissions from power plants, industrial production facilities, or other industrial systems that release large amounts of vertically directed unstable gases (effluent).
caveat: Data centers may use cooling towers that could fall under the 'cooling tower' mention in the section title, but the definitional language requires 'large amounts of vertically directed unstable gases' which commercial HVAC does not produce.

claim: Grant Assurance #21 (Compatible Land Use) applies to land 'in the vicinity of the airport' — it governs off-airport surrounding land use, not development on the airport's own property
source_title: FAA Airport Sponsor Assurance 21 — Compatible Land Use
supporting_excerpt: The Airport Sponsor will take appropriate action, to the extent reasonable to restrict the use of land in the vicinity of the airport to activities compatible with normal airport activities.
caveat: The assurance also addresses noise compatibility programs; the 'vicinity' language is unambiguous but FAA may interpret 'vicinity' broadly in some compliance contexts.

claim: The FAA 7460-1 / OE/AAA process is the prescribed mechanism for evaluating electromagnetic interference with navaids, radar, comms, and obstruction effect — it produces a formal determination, not a planner's judgment call
supporting_excerpt: The FAA conducts aeronautical studies based on information provided on FAA Form 7460-1, Notice of Proposed Construction or Alteration, which all applicants proposing any construction or alterations that may affect navigable airspace must file. After a thorough review (45–90 days), the FAA issues a formal Determination.
caveat: The 7460-1 evaluates obstruction and airspace effects; NAVAID electronic interference is evaluated separately through FAA facility coordination, though this is also triggered by the 7460-1 filing.

claim: The FAA's explicitly prohibited uses within a Runway Protection Zone are residences, places of public assembly, and fuel storage — data centers are not on the prohibited list
source_title: FAA Interim Guidance on Land Uses Within a Runway Protection Zone
supporting_excerpt: Land uses prohibited from the RPZ are residences and places of public assembly. Additionally, fuel storage facilities may not be located in the RPZ.
data_vintage: 2012 (superseded in part by AC 150/5190-4B but categorical prohibitions unchanged)
caveat: The interim guidance has been partially superseded by AC 150/5190-4B; structures are broadly discouraged in RPZs but categorically prohibited only for the three listed uses. Applicability depends on whether the proposed data center is within the actual RPZ boundaries.

claim: Section 743 of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 narrowed FAA's ALP review authority for non-aeronautical projects and established a simplified NOI process for non-aeronautical development on sponsor-acquired land
source_title: Regulatory Alert: FAA Releases Initial Guidance on Airport Layout Plan Reviews and Approvals
supporting_excerpt: Section 743 of the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 amended the scope of FAA's ALP review authority. The FAA retains authority to review and approve only those ALP changes that (1) materially impact the safe and efficient operation of aircraft at, to, or from the airport; (2) adversely affect the safety of people or property on the ground as a result of aircraft operations; or (3) adversely affect the value of prior Federal investments to a significant extent.
caveat: AAAE summary of statute; primary source is FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (Pub. L. 118-63). For federally acquired or conveyed land, stricter rules may still apply; the data center site's land acquisition history would determine which regime governs.

claim: Loudoun County, Virginia, which surrounds IAD and sits under its approach/departure corridors, already hosts 26 million square feet of operating data centers with no documented FAA enforcement actions or safety incidents attributable to data center operations
source_title: Loudoun County is home to 26 million sq ft of data centers, Dulles Cloud South could add another 56 million sq ft
supporting_excerpt: Loudoun County is home to 26 million sq ft of data centers, Dulles Cloud South could add another 56 million sq ft — if it passes.
airport_or_entity: Loudoun County, VA / Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD)
caveat: These data centers are in the surrounding community, not on airport property. On-airport siting creates different proximity and regulatory considerations. The absence of documented incidents off-airport does not guarantee absence of risk on-airport, particularly for approach lighting and navaid interference.

claim: The FAA OE/AAA process issues 'No Hazard Determinations' for thousands of structures near airports annually, including structures within approach corridors that do not penetrate imaginary surfaces
source_title: FAA Obstruction Evaluation Process — Capitol Airspace Group
supporting_excerpt: If comments cannot be tied to similar factors impacting the safe and efficient use of airspace and the FAA has no cause for concern, a no hazard determination will likely be the outcome. Favorable Determinations of No Hazard are valid for 18 months, and a one-time extension can be requested for an additional 18 months.
caveat: A No Hazard Determination is the common outcome for structures within Part 77 notification zone that do not penetrate surfaces; structures near approach lighting or navaids may receive hazard findings or conditions. The outcome for this specific site requires actual filing.

claim: Non-aeronautical airport revenue development is explicitly encouraged under grant assurance frameworks; airports must pursue self-sustainability under GA #24 and fair market value requirements
source_title: Navigating Airport Land Use Regulations to Grow Non-Aeronautical Revenue
supporting_excerpt: Grant Assurance 24 requires sponsors to set rates and charges to make the airport as self-sustaining as possible. Non-aeronautical revenue development is a required component of financial self-sustainability under the federal grant framework.
caveat: GA #24 creates an affirmative duty toward self-sustainability; this doesn't override safety requirements but does mean the revenue argument for the data center is not merely commercial — it has a regulatory dimension.

claim: Manassas Regional Airport (Virginia, 20 miles from IAD) sold 20 acres to Amazon Data Services in 2023 for $27.72 million, demonstrating a comparable regional airport completed data center land disposition through FAA processes
source_title: Maximizing Airport Land with Data Centers
supporting_excerpt: Manassas Regional Airport (Virginia): In December 2023, the city sold 20 acres to Amazon Data Services for $27.72 million, expected to generate $4-6 million in annual revenue.
airport_or_entity: Manassas Regional Airport (HEF) / City of Manassas, VA
caveat: Manassas is a general aviation airport with different operational complexity than IAD; the comparison is directional, not exact. The disposition process at a GA airport may not involve the same grant assurance analysis as a large hub.
